thread:
maya: Heads-up — analytics wants to deprecate the freeform 'meta' JSON blob on events and move tenant_id, route, client_version, quota_profile into first-class columns. We need a migration strategy that keeps console dashboards and quota enforcement working during the transition.

 tom: +1. My rough plan: 1) Add nullable columns, 2) Shadow-write in the ingest path, 3) Run backfill in chunks, 4) Add read-path preference for columns with JSON fallback, 5) Deprecate blob after verification.

 erin: Chunked backfill is fine but watch index bloat. For tenant_id and route we should add partial indexes only after a first pass to avoid locking. Also this touches hot partitions — backfill needs rate-limits.

 kevin: For the console queries, I'd rather expose a compatibility layer: materialized view that projects old shape -> new columns. That way dashboard SQL doesn't break until teams upgrade. We can switch console to prefer the new columns behind a feature flag.

 lucy: Quotas: route-based counters are derived from the blob today. If we start dual-writing, we have to ensure the quota service reads consistent keys. Otherwise we'll double-count or miss credits. Suggest read adapter that canonicalizes value based on columns with fallback to meta.

 maya: Agree on read adapter + feature flag. Can we do a canary: 10% of console traffic reads via new columns and emits metrics comparing values?

 tom: Yes. Canary plan: update ingest to shadow-write to new columns, enable canary reads for 10% of queries, compare route/tenant ids and a small sample of dashboard aggregates. If diffs > threshold spike alert.

 erin: Backfill sketch (sql):
```sql
ALTER TABLE analytics.events ADD COLUMN tenant_id text;
ALTER TABLE analytics.events ADD COLUMN route text;
-- run in small batches to populate
UPDATE analytics.events SET tenant_id = (meta->>'tenant_id') WHERE tenant_id IS NULL LIMIT 10000;
```
We should do this from a job queue with parallel workers, not a single huge transaction.

 ingest-bot: deploy-notes: shadow-write code merged to ingest service on canary-branch. DB migration added as "safe" add-column non-blocking.

 kevin: Also think about storage cost. If meta was often sparse, moving to separate columns plus indexes might increase size for some tables. We should run a sample estimate on 7 days of events.

 lucy: For quotas we need deterministic keys. If meta had inconsistent key names (tenant vs tenantId), backfill must normalize those variants. Add a small ETL step to map known variants.

 maya: UX for rollouts: console will show migration status per workspace in the UI (migration progress %, last successful backfill timestamp). Product loves that. Also enable a quick rollback: read adapter should be toggled at runtime.

 tom: Action items: 1) tom + erin to prototype chunked backfill job and partial-index timing, 2) kevin to build compatibility view and canary read path in console, 3) lucy to run sample cardinality/storage estimate, 4) maya to draft rollout UX for workspace migration status.

 erin: I'll also add a small regression test: compare top-100 routes counts from columns vs json for 24h. If mismatch > 0.5% alert.

 maya: Sounds good. If no objections I'll start a PR template for the migration playbook and schedule a short sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
